slides.texte_overlay:
hobbies that will make you
dangerously confident

the first goodbye

this week, be the one who ends conversations, with a warm "so good talking to you". people who leave on their own terms are remembered as confident, never as the one who lingered.

asking to be taught

once a week, ask someone to show you something they're good at, in person, from a recipe to a guitar chord. admitting you don't know is a power move only confident people can afford.

unedited messages

once a day, send the message you'd normally rewrite five times, as it is. most of what feels risky to say is just honest, and honest is rarely a mistake.

five minutes of everything

give 5 minutes a day to learning something random: art, history, science, psychology. confident people don't know everything, they're just never afraid of a new topic.
slides.texte_sophia:
five minutes of everything

give 5 minutes a day to learning something random: art, history, science. a micro-learning app like the Sophia app makes it easy, and you'll stop being afraid of any new topic.

slides.texte_overlay:
thank you in person

this week, say one thank you or compliment face to face instead of by text. saying kind things to someone's face is harder than criticism, and it builds more.
